title: Agentic Systems Architect
notes: Design-altitude track for production agentic AI systems. Module spine is the production-hardening 'altitude gap' that intro agent courses skip. Build-altitude fundamentals (agent loops, framework mechanics, RAG implementation) are owned by the lower-level `agentic-ai-engineer` track (level 30) and linked, not duplicated. Languages: examples in both TypeScript/Node.js and Python. Derived generically from the broad agentic-architect market (consulting/SI, enterprise-platform, security/governance, and product-agent archetypes); not anchored to any single employer, sector, or tool.

modules.title: Agentic Systems Foundations & When NOT to Use an Agent
objectives: Distinguish workflows from agents and justify the choice per task (predictability vs. model-driven flexibility)
Apply Anthropic's orchestration patterns: prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer
Decompose a system into tool vs. sub-agent vs. hardcoded-path boundaries
Frame the 'start simple, add complexity only when it demonstrably improves outcomes' discipline

modules.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration Architecture
objectives: Design orchestrator-worker topologies and reason about their token economics (~15x cost vs. single chat)
Choose between handoffs and manager-as-tools; decide who owns the final user-facing answer
Apply inter-agent protocols (MCP for tools, A2A for delegation) at architecture level
Define escalation and coordination strategies across a multi-agent system

modules.title: Memory & Context Architecture
objectives: Architect context engineering strategies: compaction, structured note-taking, sub-agent isolation, just-in-time retrieval
Diagnose and mitigate context rot in long-horizon agents
Decide where state lives: working/episodic/long-term memory and persistence boundaries
Integrate RAG and vector/knowledge-graph stores as an architectural concern

modules.title: Evaluation Harnesses for Agentic Systems
objectives: Design trajectory evaluation (sequence of messages/tool calls) and final-state evaluation
Build tool-call correctness checks at selection and argument layers (deterministic + LLM-judge)
Author LLM-as-judge rubrics (accuracy, completeness, citation, tool efficiency)
Define an offline/online eval strategy that gates deployment

modules.title: Observability & Tracing for Agents
objectives: Instrument agents with OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (invoke_agent, execute_tool spans, token attributes)
Distinguish agent observability (output quality, faithfulness, safety, drift) from traditional APM
Architect tracing for non-deterministic, long-running agents across deploys
Evaluate platforms (LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix) against requirements

modules.title: Guardrails, Safety & Security
objectives: Design two-sided input/output moderation and per-tool-call guardrails
Mitigate OWASP LLM01:2025 (prompt injection, incl. indirect) and LLM06:2025 (excessive agency)
Apply least-privilege tool access, tool sandboxing, and human approval for high-risk actions
Architect secure authentication and authorization for agent toolchains: OAuth flows, token management, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
Design sandboxing and strict permission scopes for local and remote agent/CLI execution to prevent destructive actions or data leakage
Architect segregation of untrusted content and adversarial testing into the system

modules.title: Cost & Latency Architecture
objectives: Model token economics for multi-agent systems and set value thresholds for agentic vs. workflow designs
Apply prompt/prefix caching, model routing, and batch processing as architectural levers
Build cost models and SLAs into a reference architecture
Trade off latency, cost, and quality with explicit budgets

modules.title: Deployment, Durable Execution & Human-in-the-Loop
objectives: Architect durable execution and resumption for long-running, stateful agents (e.g., Temporal)
Design deployment strategies that avoid disrupting in-flight agents (e.g., rainbow deployments)
Integrate human-in-the-loop approval flows (approve/edit/reject/respond) with state persistence
Plan scaling and failure recovery for agent fleets

modules.title: Governance, Compliance & Regulated-Domain Architecture
objectives: Apply horizontal AI governance/risk frameworks (ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act risk tiers) to an agentic architecture
Translate generic regulated-domain constraints — data privacy, residency, auditability, accountability, retention — into architecture, independent of any single statute
Map one architecture against multiple regulatory regimes and reason about where controls converge vs. diverge
Govern agent extensions/plugins/tools: how they are evaluated, versioned, approved, and monitored to prevent unauthorized change or quality drift
Produce governance, accountability, and risk-control specifications (model/data lineage, audit trails, human-accountability points) for an agent fleet

modules.title: Agentic Developer & Internal Platforms
objectives: Design an extensible agent-platform architecture using a generic extension model (agents, skills/tools, hooks/lifecycle events, MCP), mapping the concepts across at least two real platforms

Architect agents that interface securely with internal toolchains and proprietary data to perform real work (analysis, generation, debugging, operations) — with SDLC as one worked example, not the only context
Build reliable tool-use and context-hydration patterns that give an agent precise, scoped system access
Integrate with core workflow toolchains (VCS, issue trackers, knowledge bases, CI/CD) over REST, GraphQL, and event-driven interfaces
Design platform-level developer experience: onboarding, adoption, documentation, versioning, and feedback loops

projects.title: Capstone: End-to-End Agentic Reference Architecture
projects.description: Design (and prototype the orchestration of) a production agentic system of the learner's choice — e.g., a deep-research agent, a data-operations agent, or a customer-facing assistant — that exercises every module: orchestrator-workers topology, memory/context engineering, a trajectory + tool-call eval harness, OTel tracing, two-sided guardrails, a cost/latency model, durable execution, human-in-the-loop, and a horizontal governance spec. Deliverables: an ADR set, reference diagram, eval plan, cost model, and threat model. Domain is learner-selected and not pre-anchored to any one sector.

projects.title: Regulated-Domain Agentic Architecture (Learner-Selected Sector)
projects.description: Produce a reference architecture for an agentic system under regulated-domain constraints, where the learner picks one sector from a balanced menu — healthcare (HIPAA), finance (GLBA/SOX/PCI), public sector, or edtech (FERPA/COPPA) — then writes a portability analysis showing which controls change if the same system were deployed in a different listed sector. Required across all choices: data-handling/residency controls, auditability and accountability, human-in-the-loop on high-risk output, hallucination containment grounded in vetted sources, and toggleable AI features. No single sector is privileged.

projects.title: Extensible Agent Platform (Platform-Neutral)
projects.description: Design an extensible agent platform that lets agents securely interface with internal toolchains and proprietary data to perform real work. Target a generic host/extension model and justify it against at least one alternative platform (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, LangGraph Platform, or custom), explicitly addressing portability and lock-in. Deliverables: extension architecture (agents/tools/hooks/MCP), secure auth & sandboxing model (OAuth/RBAC-ABAC/token lifecycle, local+remote execution isolation, prompt-injection defenses), an extension governance lifecycle, toolchain integrations (VCS/issue-tracker/knowledge-base/CI-CD), and an adoption/DX plan. The worked domain may be SDLC or a non-developer internal workflow — learner's choice.
